title: LOKAYAN 2026 – INDIAN NAVAL SHIP SUDARSHINI CONCLUDES PORT CALL AT PONTA DELGADA
body_text:
Indian Navy’s sail training ship, INS Sudarshini, concluded her port call at Ponta Delgada, Azores, on 16 Aug 2026 , as part of Lokayan 2026.
The port call witnessed professional and cultural engagements with the Portuguese Navy, strengthening maritime cooperation and camaraderie between the two navies. A formal deck reception was hosted onboard the Portuguese Navy’s sail training vessel, NRP Sagres. This was followed by a reciprocal evening deck reception onboard INS Sudarshini for local military leadership, diplomats and members of the Indian diaspora.
The ship also celebrated India’s 80th Independence Day at Ponta Delgada on 15 Aug 2026. The ship was dressed overall, and a Colours ceremony was held to mark the occasion with pride and patriotism.
INS Sudarshini has now set sail for Lisbon. On 21 Aug 2026 , INS Sudarshini and NRP Sagres are scheduled to undertake a joint Passing Exercise (PASSEX) at sea, featuring coordinated sail manoeuvres and communication drills, further strengthening interoperability and maritime cooperation between the two navies.
******
VM/AS 150/26

enrichment.summary: INS Sudarshini, the Indian Navy's sail training ship, concluded a port call at Ponta Delgada, Azores, on 16 August 2026 as part of the Lokayan 2026 deployment, holding cultural and professional exchanges with the Portuguese Navy including reciprocal deck receptions. The ship also marked India's 80th Independence Day there on 15 August with a Colours ceremony. It has now departed for Lisbon, where it will conduct a joint Passing Exercise (PASSEX) with Portuguese Navy vessel NRP Sagres on 21 August 2026.
enrichment.context: INS Sudarshini is a sail training ship of the Indian Navy used for training cadets in traditional seamanship and for goodwill/cultural diplomacy voyages abroad, often called 'sail diplomacy'. Lokayan 2026 appears to be one such overseas deployment aimed at showcasing India's naval heritage, strengthening bilateral defence ties, and engaging the Indian diaspora abroad. Such port calls and PASSEX exercises are routine components of naval diplomacy, building interoperability and goodwill rather than representing major policy or strategic shifts.
